newsitem.title: CANADA: Teck loses bid for Kazakhstan mine deal.
newsitem.headline: Teck loses bid for Kazakhstan mine deal.

text.p: Canadian mining company Teck Corp said late Friday that the Kazakhstan government's tender commission had rejected a proposal from it and First Dynasty Mines Ltd to develop the Vasilkovskoye gold deposit.
Investors had long awaited news on the project which has been dogged by controversy.

In a brief statement, Teck said the two companies "respected the decision of the tender commission and remained interested in mining exploration and development in Kazakhstan including the possibility of reopening negotiations on Vasilkovskoye should opportunities become available."
Teck officials were not available for further comment.

Teck had won a tender in June to negotiate a deal to develop the Vasilkovskoye deposit in northern Kazakhstan which has 14 million ounces of gold reserves. But that broke down in August after a dispute with the government over a proposed investment plan.

The government subsequently returned the right to Teck in October to negotiate a deal on the deposit, but talks between the companies and the government were difficult, officials have previously said.
Teck said in November it appeared to be making progress on resolving outstanding issues with the government such as taxation, infrastructure and ownership rights on the deposit.

The deposit had also been embroiled in controversy before. Placer Dome Inc won rights to the project in 1995 after the Kazakhstan government bypassed a tender organized by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
Placer later pulled out, saying conditions of the agreement had not been met. Kazakhstan then organized a tender which resulted in the first Teck deal.
Placer is still seeking the return of a US$35 million deposit from the Kazakhstan government.
